documentation.range: Megupsilon aporus was once restricted to the Potosi Spring northwest of Galeana in Nuevo Leon, Mexico. This species was considered Extinct in the Wild (EW) as a result of total habitat loss, and has not been recorded at this locality since 1994 (Valdés González et al. 2018). However, there are no known captive populations, as the last remaining captive population was lost in 2012 (Lozano-Vilano and Maza-Benignos 2017, A. Eschelle pers. comm. 2018, C. Martin pers. comm. 2018).
documentation.population: Megupsilon aporus has not been recorded in the wild since 1994 (Burkhead 2012, Lozano-Vilano and Maza-Benignos 2017, Valdés González et al. 2018). Surveys have been conducted in nearby springs, but it has not been recorded.
documentation.habitats: Historical habitat included clear springs and spring-fed ditches in the presence of dense aquatic macrophytes over clay, mud, firm limestone and sandy substrates (Miller et al. 2005). Water temperature fluctuated annually from 16.5-23 oC. Potosi springs was at 1880 m elevation (Miller et al. 2005).
documentation.threats: Major threats that led to the extirpation of M. aporus in the wild include a near total loss of habitat resulting from groundwater extraction, and the impacts of predatory and competitive introduced species (Contreras-Balderas and Lozano-Vilano 1996, Miller et al. 2005).
documentation.measures: The last remaining captive population of M. aporus was lost in 2012 (Lozano-Vilano and Maza-Benignos 2017, Valdés González et al. 2018).  Genetic tissue has been preserved for this species (A. Valdes pers. comm. 2018).
documentation.use_trade: There is no information about the past use and trade of this species.
documentation.rationale: Megupsilon aporus was once restricted to the Potosi Spring northwest of Galeana in Nuevo Leon, Mexico. This species is now considered Extinct (EX) as a result of total habitat loss, and has not been recorded at this locality since 1994. There are no known captive populations. The last remaining captive population was lost in 2012.
